keyVerseText: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
rootMeaning: The word πρᾶγμα (prâgma) derives from the verb πράσσω (prássō), which means to perform or carry out actions repeatedly or habitually. This root sense emphasizes not just a single act but the execution or practice of deeds, highlighting a dynamic and ongoing engagement with tasks or affairs. Thus, πρᾶγμα conveys a tangible reality of things done or matters actively handled, extending beyond a mere abstract concept to include concrete acts and their results.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, πρᾶγμα appears eleven times and is translated variously as 'thing,' 'business,' 'matter,' or 'affair,' reflecting its broad semantic range. It can denote a concrete object or deed, as well as an abstract matter or legal case, showing flexibility in usage. This variety of translations reveals that πρᾶγμα encompasses both tangible realities and ongoing activities or concerns, underscoring its function as a term for what is done or what requires attention in life and faith.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πρᾶγμα enriches our grasp of biblical teaching by reminding us that faith engages with real, concrete matters and actions, not just abstract ideas. The word's root in habitual practice points to the importance of consistent obedience and lived-out faith, not merely isolated acts. Theologically, this highlights that God cares about the deeds and affairs of His people, encompassing both their spiritual and practical lives. Recognizing πρᾶγμα's scope encourages believers to approach their daily actions and decisions as meaningful in God's kingdom purpose.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 18:19 states, 'Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.' Here, πρᾶγμα as 'any thing' emphasizes the tangible realities or matters believers bring before God in prayer. It underscores the concrete nature of their requests and the assurance that God actively responds to these real concerns. This affirms a faith that trusts God’s power to act decisively on the affairs and deeds that His people present to Him in unity.
